results.name: EZ Bar Biceps Curl Wide Grip
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ bar with hands just wider than shoulder-width, palms facing forward, and your arms fully extended down.
Curl the EZ bar towards your chest by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary and close to your body.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, ensuring the bar reaches shoulder height.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on engaging your biceps throughout the movement.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize biceps activation and reduce injury risk.
Exhale as you curl the bar up and inhale as you lower it back down.
results.description: EZ Bar Biceps Curl Wide Grip is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with an ez barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

Curl the EZ bar towards your shoulder by bending your elbows, keeping your upper arms stationary and close to your body.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, ensuring the bar reaches shoulder height.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

results.description: EZ Bar Cable Curl Wide Grip is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with an ez barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: EZ Barbell Close Grip Curl
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding an EZ barbell with a close grip (hands positioned closer than shoulder-width apart) and palms facing up.
Curl the barbell upward towards your shoulders by bending your elbows, focusing on engaging your biceps.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, ensuring the barbell reaches shoulder height.
Lower the barbell back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms.
tips: Keep your elbows stationary and close to your body throughout the movement.
Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to lift the barbell.
Exhale as you curl the barbell up and inhale as you lower it.

results.name: Hammer Curl Resistance Band Simultaneous
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, placing the resistance band under both feet. Hold the handles with your palms facing each other and your arms extended down at your sides.
Curl the handles up towards your shoulders simultaneously by bending your elbows, keeping your palms facing each other throughout the movement.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your elbows close to your body and avoid swinging your arms.
Focus on engaging your biceps and forearms throughout the movement.
Exhale as you curl the handles up and inhale as you lower them back down.
results.description: Hammer Curl Resistance Band Simultaneous is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a band, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Hammer Strength MTS Iso-Lateral Biceps Curl Arm Alternating
instructions: Sit on the Hammer Strength MTS Iso-Lateral Biceps Curl machine with your feet flat on the floor. Grasp the handles with both hands, palms facing up, and position your elbows on the pads.
Curl one handle by bending your elbow, bringing your hand towards your shoulder while keeping the other arm extended.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement and slowly lower the handle back to the starting position with control.
Repeat with the other arm, alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you curl the handle up and inhale as you lower it back down.
Maintain a neutral wrist position to prevent strain.
Focus on engaging your biceps throughout the movement.
results.description: Hammer Strength MTS Iso-Lateral Biceps Curl Arm Alternating is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement and slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control.

Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement and slowly lower the handle back to the starting position with control.

results.name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to a 45-degree incline and sit back against it with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended down by your sides, palms facing forward (supinated grip).
Engage your core and keep your elbows close to your torso. Slowly curl both dumbbells up towards your shoulders simultaneously, maintaining the supinated grip with your palms facing upward.
Squeeze your biceps at the top of the movement, then slowly lower the dumbbells back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on a full range of motion, ensuring you fully extend your arms at the bottom of each curl.
Maintain a slight bend in your elbows at the start to avoid locking them out.
Keep your upper arms stationary and close to your torso to isolate the biceps effectively.
results.description: Incline Dumbbell Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.

results.name: Kettlebell Concentration Curl
instructions: Sit near the front of a flat bench with your feet wider than shoulder width apart. Hold a kettlebell in your left hand using an underhand grip, brace your elbow against the inside of your left thigh, and rest your right hand on your right thigh.
Keep your upper arm still and curl the kettlebell toward your shoulder, by bending your elbow.
Pause briefly at the top and squeeze your biceps without lifting your elbow from your thigh.
Lower the kettlebell until your arm is extended, then repeat before switching sides.
tips: Lean forward slightly while keeping your back straight.
Avoid moving your upper arm as you curl.
Maintain an underhand grip with your wrist straight.
Exhale as you curl and inhale as you lower.
results.description: Kettlebell Concentration Curl is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with a kettlebell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Forearms.
